articles.title: Nvidia Study: AI Agents Rarely Need Long Context Windows
articles.summary: NVIDIA researchers find Claude Opus 4.5 and GPT 5.6 Sol lose little accuracy with 16K contexts and frequent compaction, while long-context serving costs up to 7x more per token. Long context windows are one of the main selling points of frontier models. A new preprint from NVIDIA, titled “You don’t need long context”, questions whether agents actually need them. Peter Belcak, Pavlo Molchanov and ten co-authors test what happens when models must keep their working context short, by regularly summarizing their own history, and conclude that the long-context race may be solving the wrong problem.

articles.title: See the agents, set the terms: new visibility and control for personal agents
articles.summary: Personal agents are the intermediary between humans and the Internet, turning a person’s instructions into requests and actions on websites. A customer might ask a personal agent to compare products across your site, find support articles, or complete a purchase. To a site owner, all three interactions show up as automated traffic — and without a clear view of which agents are visiting and what they are doing, it can be difficult to know whether that traffic is helping your business or creating risk. Blocking agents altogether can feel like the safest choice, but it can mean losing customers.
